27.solution_text: By conservation of mechanical energy, \((ME)_i=(ME)_f\) and \(PE_i+KE_i=PE_f+KE_f\). Thus \(0+7.9\times10^6\times1.6\times10^{-19}=\frac{k(2e)(Ze)}{r}+0\). Using \(k=9\times10^9\), \(Z=79\), and \(e=1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm C\), the source gives \(r=2.88\times10^{-14}\,\mathrm m\). Therefore the diameter is \(D=2r=5.76\times10^{-14}\,\mathrm m\).

45.solution_text: The magnetic field through the middle coil is \(\vec B=(B_{C_2}-B_{C_1})\hat i\). Therefore the flux is \(\phi=(B_{C_2}-B_{C_1})A\), and the induced emf is \(\varepsilon=-\frac{d\phi}{dt}\). Applying Lenz's law to the stated motion, the printed solution marks option (2) as the correct answer.

60.solution_text: Option (A): \(W=-nRT\ln\frac{V_2}{V_1}=-\frac{2\times8.314\times300}{1000}\ln\frac{20}{2}\,\mathrm{kJ}=-11.5\,\mathrm{kJ}\). Option (B): \(W=-P_{\mathrm{ext}}(V_2-V_1)=-3(3-1)=-6\,\mathrm{kJ}\). Option (C): \(\Delta U=nC_V\Delta T=1\times\frac32\times\frac{8.314\times320}{1000}\,\mathrm{kJ}\approx3.99\,\mathrm{kJ}\). Option (D): \(\Delta H=nC_P\Delta T=1\times\frac52\times\frac{8.314\times337}{1000}\,\mathrm{kJ}\approx7\,\mathrm{kJ}\).

72.solution_text: The standard cell potential is \(E^\circ_{\mathrm{cell}}=-0.44-(-0.90)=+0.46\,\mathrm V\). Applying the Nernst equation, \(E_{\mathrm{cell}}=E^\circ_{\mathrm{cell}}-\frac{0.06}{n}\log Q\). Substituting \(n=6\) and \(Q=10^6\), \(E_{\mathrm{cell}}=0.46-\frac{0.06}{6}\log10^6=4\times10^{-1}\,\mathrm V\). Thus \(x=4\).

73.solution_text: Equating the rate constants gives \(10^4e^{-24000/T}=10^6e^{-30000/T}\). Hence \(e^{6000/T}=100\), so \(\frac{6000}{T}=2\ln10\). Therefore \(T=\frac{6000}{2\times2.303}=1302.64\,\mathrm K\), or approximately \(1303\,\mathrm K\).

74.solution_text: Iodine gives the violet colour. The halogen percentage is calculated as \(\%I=\frac{\text{atomic weight of I}}{\text{molecular weight of AgI}}\times\frac{m}{W}\times100\). Thus \(\%I=\frac{127}{235}\times\frac{0.12}{0.15}\times100=43.23\%\approx43\%\).

75.solution_text: For the dissociation, the source evaluates \(\Delta G^\circ_{\mathrm{rxn}}=-1.664\times10^3\,\mathrm J=-8.3\times300\ln K_p\). This gives \(\ln K_p=0.693\) and \(K_p=2\). Using \(2=\frac{4\alpha^2P_0}{1-\alpha^2}\) at \(P_0=1\) bar gives \(\alpha=\frac1{\sqrt3}\). Since \(\alpha=(x\times10^{-2})^{1/2}\), \(x=\frac{100}{3}\approx33.33\), so the nearest integer is \(33\).
